summary: A Chinese supercar shattered the industry ceiling with a top speed of 503.17 km/h, Zeekr hit its 300,000-unit annual sales target early, and a wave of new models — including the Geely Xingyuan, Lynk & Co 08 EM-P, Peugeot 408 and Aeolus L8+ — launched in quick succession.

articles.title: 503.17 km/h! Chinese Supercar Shatters Top-Speed Record, Redefining Performance Limits
articles.summary: A Chinese supercar hit a top speed of 503.17 km/h, breaking the 500 km/h barrier for the first time and entering the global supercar elite in terms of performance.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, a Chinese supercar clocked a top speed of 503.17 km/h, shattering the 500 km/h threshold long dominated by top European and American supercar brands. For years, global top-speed records have largely been held by makers such as Bugatti, Koenigsegg, SSC and Hennessey, while Chinese brands, lacking a signature performance halo in the supercar space, have typically marketed electrification and smart features instead. The 503.17 km/h result shows that Chinese automakers now have the capability to compete with the world's best supercars across core engineering disciplines, including powertrain, aerodynamics, tire formulation, body rigidity and chassis calibration. Technically, breaking 500 km/h places extreme demands on sustained power delivery, high-speed stability and braking thermal management, often requiring in-house development of battery-electric or high-performance hybrid architectures as well as long-term investment in wind-tunnel and track validation programs.
articles.impact: Provides a landmark performance endorsement for Chinese auto brands seeking to move upmarket, breaks the European and American dominance narrative in the supercar segment, and helps drive brand premiums and win over high-end consumers.

articles.title: Zeekr Delivers Over 320,000 Units in First 10 Months, Beating 300,000 Annual Target Early
articles.summary: Zeekr delivered more than 320,000 units from January to October, exceeding its full-year target of 300,000 two months ahead of schedule.
articles.detail: According to Sogou News, Zeekr's cumulative deliveries from January to October this year have topped 320,000 units, surpassing the full-year target of 300,000 ahead of schedule. This means the company locked in its annual KPI by the end of October, with sales in the final two months essentially adding on top of it. Against the backdrop of intensifying competition and recurring price wars in the NEV market, Zeekr's early achievement is closely tied to the continued expansion of its product lineup, faster iteration of refreshed models, and a denser retail network. At the current pace, Zeekr's full-year deliveries could reach the 350,000-unit range, further consolidating its position at the top of the premium BEV segment. As Geely Group's brand focused on premium new-energy vehicles, Zeekr's growth also provides a key incremental boost to Geely's overall NEV transition, complementing the Geely Xingyuan and Lynk & Co EM-P series to form a product lineup spanning high and low price points.
articles.impact: Signals that the premium BEV market still has room to grow, provides strong support for Geely Group's full-year NEV sales, and raises capital-market expectations for Zeekr's profitability.

articles.title: Geely Xingyuan STAR Limited Series Launched at 88,800 Yuan for a Limited Time
articles.summary: Geely Xingyuan launched the STAR limited series at a promotional price of 88,800 yuan, pushing further into the A0-segment BEV price band.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, Geely has officially launched the Xingyuan STAR limited series at a limited-time promotional price of 88,800 yuan. As Geely's volume model in the A0-segment electric mini-car market, the Xingyuan has enjoyed steady sales since launch thanks to its efficient use of space, generous equipment, and competitive pricing. The STAR limited series aims to sustain that momentum through a differentiated version. The 88,800-yuan price further lowers the Xingyuan's entry threshold into the mainstream A0 BEV competitive range, directly targeting popular small cars such as the BYD Seagull and Wuling Bingo. From a market-strategy perspective, limited editions typically offer personalized tweaks to exterior colors, interior details, and configuration bundles to suit the tastes of young first-time buyers. In the critical fourth-quarter push for volume, Geely's combination of a limited edition and a limited-time price is expected to further widen the Xingyuan's share advantage in the entry-level BEV market.
articles.impact: Intensifies competition in the A0 BEV segment, puts direct pricing pressure on similarly priced rivals, and benefits budget-conscious first-time buyers.

articles.title: 2027 Lynk & Co 08 EM-P Launched at 159,800 Yuan for Limited-Time Trade-In
articles.summary: The 2027 Lynk & Co 08 EM-P officially launched with a limited-time trade-in price starting at 159,800 yuan, strengthening its competitiveness in the midsize plug-in hybrid SUV segment.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, the 2027 Lynk & Co 08 EM-P has officially launched with a limited-time trade-in price starting at 159,800 yuan. The 08 EM-P is the brand's core model in the midsize PHEV SUV market, built on the CMA Evo architecture and equipped with the EM-P super range-extended electric system, catering to both electric commuting and long-distance travel. The 2027 model features configuration upgrades and, thanks to the limited-time trade-in price, brings the entry point below 160,000 yuan, cutting directly into the core price band of rivals such as the BYD Tang DM-i and Deepal S07. The trade-in offer also reflects automakers' sharper fight over existing owners looking to upgrade in the fourth quarter, using trade-in subsidies and stacked benefits to drive replacement purchases. Overall, the pricing strategy of the 08 EM-P continues the Geely group's broader playbook this year: trading price for volume to hold NEV market share.
articles.impact: Intensifies price competition in midsize PHEV SUVs, gives replacement buyers waiting on the sidelines a more cost-effective option, and pressures rivals to match the concessions.

articles.title: Dongfeng Aeolus L8+ Launched From 129,900 Yuan With 700 TOPS ADAS Compute
articles.summary: The Dongfeng Aeolus L8+ launched at 129,900 yuan with 700 TOPS of ADAS computing power, bringing advanced driver assistance to the 120,000-yuan segment.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, the Dongfeng Aeolus L8+ has officially launched at 129,900 yuan, with its biggest highlight being an intelligent driving system delivering 700 TOPS of computing power. Compute at the 700 TOPS level previously appeared mostly in mid-to-high-end NEV models priced above 200,000 yuan; bringing it down to the 120,000-yuan segment with the L8+ reflects the industry trend of rapidly falling hardware costs and faster adoption. The high-compute platform leaves ample headroom for highway navigation assist, urban assisted driving, and future OTA upgrades, meaning entry-level users can enjoy an experience close to that of advanced ADAS. Dongfeng Aeolus's decision to use computing power as its selling point in the compact segment aligns with its overall NEV transition and underscores the urgency with which traditional automakers are catching up with new EV entrants in the intelligence race.
articles.impact: Drives advanced ADAS hardware down into the 120,000-yuan market, accelerates the democratization of intelligent driving, and delivers an outsized blow to same-priced models lacking ADAS capability.

articles.title: Range Rover Launches Three Special Editions From ¥1.498 Million, With Just 3 Collector's Editions Worldwide
articles.summary: Land Rover unveils three special edition Range Rover models starting at ¥1.498 million, with the Collector's Edition limited to just 3 units globally.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, Land Rover has officially launched three special edition Range Rover models, starting at ¥1.498 million, with the Collector's Edition limited to just 3 units worldwide. As a benchmark product in the luxury full-size SUV segment, Range Rover has long relied on SV customization and limited special editions to preserve brand exclusivity and its upscale positioning. The three editions, launched simultaneously, cover different exterior color schemes, interior materials and dedicated equipment combinations, with the Collector's Edition further enhancing its collectible appeal through an extremely tight production quota. Amid overall pressure on the luxury car market and broadly deepening dealer discounts, Jaguar Land Rover has chosen limited-edition customization over price cuts to defend Range Rover's brand premium — a classic high-end value operation strategy. For ultra-luxury buyers, scarcity itself is part of a product's value.
articles.impact: Provides a scarcity-driven product benchmark for the ultra-luxury SUV market, reinforces Range Rover's premium brand image, and differentiates it from the price war tactics of mainstream luxury brands.

articles.title: Global Top-Speed Order Shifts: 503.17 km/h Record Redraws the Supercar Performance Map
articles.summary: A Chinese supercar hits 503.17 km/h, rewriting the global supercar performance map long dominated by European and American brands.
articles.detail: Reporting via NetEase Auto, a Chinese supercar has posted a top speed of 503.17 km/h, putting a Chinese entrant into the top tier of global production and prototype supercar speed rankings. For years, the 500 km/h-plus territory has been held by European and American models such as the Bugatti Chiron Super Sport 300+, SSC Tuatara, Koenigsegg Jesko Absolut and Hennessey Venom F5. Chinese brands have mostly entered the performance narrative through electrification advantages like 0-100 km/h acceleration and lap times, leaving top-speed records blank. This breakthrough not only changes how global media perceive the performance ceiling of Chinese cars, but also prompts overseas supercar makers to reassess Chinese brands' technical depth in powertrain engineering and extreme-condition validation. From an industry perspective, the significance of such a record lies not in volume, but in technology spillover — thermal management, materials and aerodynamics solutions proven under extreme conditions can gradually trickle down to mainstream road cars.
articles.impact: Reshapes the global supercar competition narrative, gives Chinese brands international voice in their premium push, and technology spillover from extreme engineering is expected to lift the technical standards of mainstream road cars.

articles.title: Road-Tested at 3.6L/100km: Changan CS75 PLUS Blue Whale Super Engine Fuel Economy In-Depth
articles.summary: Real-world testing puts the Changan CS75 PLUS Blue Whale Super Engine edition at just 3.6L/100km combined, a significant win for its hybrid technology route.
articles.detail: According to road-test data from NetEase Auto, the Changan CS75 PLUS Blue Whale Super Engine edition delivered actual fuel consumption as low as 3.6L/100km. As the flagship SUV in Changan's gasoline and hybrid lineup, the CS75 PLUS has long been a fixture on compact SUV sales charts, and these test results show notable gains in the Blue Whale powertrain's thermal efficiency and energy management. With the penetration rate of new-energy vehicles steadily rising, conventional fuel and hybrid models must achieve extreme efficiency to retain conservative buyers who are reluctant to switch to battery-electric vehicles. A figure of 3.6L/100km is approaching the battery-depleted fuel consumption of plug-in hybrids, indicating that the internal combustion route still has considerable room for optimization through deep Miller cycle calibration, high compression ratios, and intelligent energy recovery. For family buyers, lower fuel consumption directly translates into reduced ownership costs — one of the most decisive factors in this segment.
articles.impact: Offers cost-conscious consumers who are wary of new energy a low-emission, high-value option, proving that internal combustion and hybrid powertrains remain viable in the compact SUV market.

articles.title: Exclusive Interview with Jiang Ping: No Safety Tiers — Changan Vows to Make Safety Tech Accessible to All
articles.summary: Changan Auto's Jiang Ping says safety should not be tiered by trim level, calling for safety technology to be rolled out across the entire model range.
articles.detail: In an interview with NetEase Auto, Changan Auto's Jiang Ping stated clearly that the company will not differentiate safety by trim level and aims to make safety technology universally available across its full product range. The remarks take direct aim at a widespread industry practice: advanced active safety systems, body structure materials, and airbag counts are often reserved for high-end or top-trim variants, while entry-level models see safety equipment cut back. Changan's stance is to make core technologies — including passive safety structures and active driver-assistance features — standard across all price tiers, effectively returning safety from a marketing bullet point on the spec sheet to a fundamental attribute of the vehicle. With collision test bodies such as C-IASI tightening their standards and consumer awareness of safety on the rise, this strategy both responds to regulatory trends and serves as a competitive differentiator, particularly resonating with family buyers.
articles.impact: Pushes the industry toward standard rather than optional safety equipment, forcing rivals to close safety gaps on entry-level models and benefiting long-term road safety for consumers.

articles.title: AI-Driving Compute Arms Race Begins: 700TOPS Pushed Downmarket Could Reshape the 120,000-Yuan Segment
articles.summary: The Fengshen L8+ brings 700TOPS of computing power to the 129,900-yuan price bracket, signaling that mass-market access to advanced driver-assistance will become the next competitive battleground.
articles.detail: Today's launch of the Fengshen L8+, fitted with a 700TOPS intelligent-driving system and priced from just 129,900 yuan, shows that the cost of ADAS hardware is falling faster than the industry expected. Compute at the 700TOPS level was previously the preserve of models priced above 200,000 yuan; its arrival in the 120,000-yuan segment means driving capability will no longer be a moat for mid-to-high-end cars by 2027. Looking ahead, more domestic brands are likely to make high-compute ADAS platforms standard equipment in the 100,000–150,000-yuan range, with compute, LiDAR and end-to-end large models becoming new purchase-decision factors. Meanwhile, hardware headroom will create space for future OTA upgrades, and software subscriptions and ADAS services could become new revenue streams for automakers. For consumers, this is a tangible technology dividend; for carmakers lacking in-house ADAS capability, it marks the start of a new round of elimination.
articles.impact: Signals an acceleration of ADAS democratization, with the 100,000–150,000-yuan segment becoming the main battleground and less intelligent automakers facing the risk of marginalization.

articles.title: Snowfall in Beijing, 20cm of Snow at the Great Wall: Winter Extremes Offer Lessons for Car Use and the Market
articles.summary: Beijing has seen snowfall, with snow reaching 20 centimeters deep along the Great Wall, posing new demands on driving safety and vehicle choice in extreme winter conditions.
articles.detail: According to Baidu Hot Search, snow has recently fallen in Beijing, with snow accumulation around the Great Wall reaching 20 centimeters. The first heavy snowstorm of the northern winter is a real-world test of low-temperature range, all-wheel-drive performance, thermal management and the reliability of driver-assistance systems in vehicles on sale. For new-energy vehicle owners, cold weather is the main cause of range loss, and the value of heat-pump air conditioning and battery pre-heating will be reassessed over the coming winter. For combustion and hybrid models, AWD performance and ESP calibration on low-grip surfaces are more critical. As winter deepens, automakers are expected to increase marketing around real-world cold-weather range tests and ice-and-snow road safety, boosting interest in AWD and long-range variants. Roadside assistance and after-sales service capability in extreme weather will also become a key dimension in how users judge a brand.
articles.impact: Extreme winter conditions will raise the weight of AWD, thermal management and range in purchase decisions, pushing automakers to strengthen technical validation and customer service in low-temperature scenarios.
